items.title: Nevada wildfire forces tens of thousands to evacuate as blaze threatens city of Reno
items.standfirst: Tens of thousands of people faced another night away from home on Monday as a wind-driven wildfire threatened Reno, Nevada, blanketing the city in smoke and closing schools. About 24,000 people remained under evacuation orders, down from more than 40,000 at the peak, while tens of thousands more were on alert.

items.standfirst: Tens of thousands are still under evacuation orders or warnings amid ‘human-caused’, wind-driven blazeThe Hawk fire is about 27% contained, authorities said on Monday afternoon, two days after the fast-moving, wind-driven wildfire sparked near Reno, Nevada.Authorities added that 23,000 people are under a “go-now” order and 40,000 people are under a “get-set” warning, an improvement from the 90,000 Nevadans under evacuation orders or warnings on Monday morning. items.title: Trump administration to revoke hundreds of thousands of asylum visas
items.standfirst: US President Donald Trump’s administration said on Monday it plans to revoke non-immigrant visas held by foreigners who applied for or are seeking asylum in the United States. The move could affect up to 200,000 people, the Associated Press reported, potentially making it the largest mass visa revocation in US history.

items.title: Dozens killed after rain triggers landslide at a landfill in Guinea
items.standfirst: A landslide at a landfill in Guinea left at least 30 people dead and destroyed several nearby homes after heavy rains. Days earlier, officials said the landfill would be closed because of the danger it posed, especially during the ongoing rainy season.
items.content: A landslide at a landfill in Guinea left at least 30 people dead and destroyed several nearby homes after heavy rains. Days earlier, officials said the landfill would be closed because of the danger it posed, especially during the ongoing rainy season.

items.title: Landslide at waste mound in Guinea capital kills 30, government says
items.standfirst: Dump site in Conakry, which minister had just promised to move, collapsed after heavy rain in west African stateA ⁠landslide at a huge waste dump in Guinea’s capital has killed 30 people, the government said on Sunday, after heavy rains overnight prompted it to ⁠collapse, engulfing nearby tents and shacks.The incident occurred less than a week after the government announced plans to close the ⁠site and relocate the waste because of the threat it posed, especially during the rainy season, which causes landslides and fatal flash ⁠floods each year in crowded, underdeveloped cities across parts of West Africa.
